description: "Ars Recte Vivendi; Being Essays Contributed to 'The Easy Chair'" by George William Curtis is a collection of essays likely written in the late 19th century, reflecting on various societal and moral questions relevant to that time. Through engaging prose, the author examines issues such as hygiene, manners, education, and the influence of wealth on character and social interactions, aiming to encourage readers to aspire to higher moral standards in both private and public life.
